name: Charles Watson
contribution: Admiral Charles Watson commanded Royal Navy forces that supported East India Company operations in Bengal during the campaigns of 1756–1757.
context: His naval intervention followed the British loss of Calcutta and formed part of the combined military response against Siraj ud-Daulah. Naval power supported the recovery of Calcutta and the campaign that culminated at Plassey.
impact: Watson's role shows how Royal Navy resources and Company political interests combined in the military transformation of Bengal before Plassey.
highlight: Royal Navy commander whose forces supported the British recovery of Calcutta before Plassey.
seoTitle: Charles Watson: Naval Commander in Bengal Before Plassey
seoDescription: Learn about Admiral Charles Watson and the Royal Navy support that strengthened British operations in Bengal before the Battle of Plassey.
shortAnswer: Charles Watson was a Royal Navy admiral whose forces supported British and Company operations in Bengal in 1756–1757.

faq.question: What did Charles Watson do in Bengal?
faq.answer: He commanded Royal Navy forces supporting the British recovery of Calcutta and the Company campaign before Plassey.
